tierWindow.goal: Articulate what academic integrity is and the values behind it, justify why referencing matters as scholarly practice rather than rule-following, and judge how to use sources with integrity.
tierWindow.cognitiveDemand: Articulation, justification, evaluation and judgement (articulate, justify, appraise, judge); reasoning about principles, not reciting procedures.
tierWindow.taskComplexity: Open, principled questions with defensible rather than single right answers; integrity judgements that weigh competing considerations.
tierWindow.autonomy: Low scaffolding; the learner reasons and defends a position; feedback tests the quality of reasoning rather than confirming a lookup.

decidedValue.priorExperienceAnchor: The learner already knows the mechanics of referencing: what a reference is made of, the main styles, and how to cite accurately when quoting and paraphrasing (the introductory and intermediate tiers). This course assumes that fluency and goes to the why and the judgement: the values of academic integrity, the scholarly reasons references matter, and the integrity decisions involved in using sources.

decidedValue.signpostBody: The course has three short lessons. First, academic integrity and its values: what you are really being asked to hold. Second, why referencing matters: the scholarly work a reference does, beyond keeping you out of trouble. Third, using sources with integrity: the judgement involved in quoting and paraphrasing well. Work through them in order; each builds on the one before.
decidedValue.signpostInstruction: Work through the three lessons in order.
decidedValue.overview:
This short course is about academic integrity: what it really is, why referencing matters so much to it, and how to use sources with the judgement that integrity asks for. It assumes you can already reference accurately, and steps back to the principles that referencing serves. By the end you will be able to articulate what academic integrity means, justify why referencing matters beyond avoiding plagiarism, and judge how to quote and paraphrase sources with integrity.

These are not box-ticking concerns. Integrity is what makes academic work trustworthy, and the ability to use sources with judgement is what separates confident scholarly writing from anxious rule-following. Owning it now carries into your dissertation, and into any professional work where your word has to be relied on.
decidedValue.courseOutcomesFraming: Three course outcomes framed up front: articulate academic integrity and its values, justify why referencing matters beyond avoiding plagiarism, judge how to use sources with integrity.

practiceConnection.academic: Academic integrity is the ground every piece of academic work stands on. Each essay you reference with purpose, each source you weigh rather than stack, each judgement about quoting or paraphrasing, is integrity in practice. Build the habit of owning it now and it carries through your degree and into professional work, where being trusted with the truth is the whole point.

decidedValue.summary: You have reached the end of the course. Academic integrity is no longer a rulebook but a set of values you can name and defend: honesty, trust, fairness, respect, responsibility and courage. You can articulate what integrity means and how it shows up in practice. You can justify why referencing matters as scholarly work, crediting a conversation and signalling the scope and critical edge of your reading, not merely avoiding plagiarism. And you can judge when to quote and when to paraphrase, and tell sound source use from a breach. Look back at the confidence check: comparing where you started with where you are now shows how far this has moved.

practiceConnection.academic: From here, integrity is something you practise in every piece of work. Each source you reference with purpose, each judgement about quoting or paraphrasing, each difficult case you handle by the values, is integrity owned rather than obeyed. It is also what professional life depends on: being someone whose account of where knowledge came from can be trusted.
